Ophthalmology · published research

Trabeculectomy

Two rabbit studies reported reduced filtration-site scarring and lower CTGF, PCNA, or collagen-related measures after He-Ne treatment. No human clinical outcome study is listed.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

Two rabbit studies reported reduced filtration-site scarring and lower CTGF, PCNA, or collagen-related measures after He-Ne treatment. No human clinical outcome study is listed.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact trabeculectomy category contains two 2010 publications, both rabbit studies from Chinese groups. Neither is a human clinical trial. The papers assess filtration-site scarring and associated tissue markers after surgery. Because the reports are closely related in date, methods, and research teams, animal-cohort overlap cannot be determined from the source records. Hu et al. 2010 Wang et al. 2010

Human and clinical evidence

No study in patients after trabeculectomy was identified. The available publications do not measure human bleb survival, long-term intraocular pressure, need for repeat surgery, visual function, or postoperative complications.

Animal evidence

The two rabbit experiments applied He-Ne light to the filtration area around trabeculectomy. They report less scar formation and lower expression of markers including connective-tissue growth factor, proliferating cell nuclear antigen, and collagen-related measures. These outcomes support a possible effect on postoperative wound biology in rabbits, but do not establish improvement in clinical surgical success.

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No separately listed in-vitro or ex-vivo trabeculectomy publication was identified. The reported fibroblast and tissue-marker outcomes were measured within the rabbit experiments.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

Both reports used 633 nm He-Ne light at a stated irradiance of 200 mW/cm². One source record reports ten minutes, and the other specifies 120 J/cm². These were pretreatment protocols in rabbit surgery and cannot be converted directly into a human postoperative schedule.

Interpretation

The findings are limited to preclinical wound-healing markers and come from two related publications. They do not show that PBM prevents bleb failure or improves pressure control in people. Human safety and efficacy studies are absent.

Publications and records2 animal publications (rabbit models) from 2010.

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Both publications are 2010 rabbit experiments from related Chinese research groups. They report lower scarring markers after He-Ne pretreatment, but no human trial measures bleb survival, intraocular pressure, or surgical success. The studies may use related methods or cohorts, which are not deduplicated.

Publication and study types

  • The papers report preclinical tissue and scarring outcomes and may share related methods or animal cohorts, but overlap cannot be established.
  • No human participants, clinical trials, in-vitro, or ex-vivo studies are listed.
